## Why

RStudio gave you one R session per project. VS Code made you pick a Python interpreter per window. Positron runs several sessions of both languages at once, and that is where people lose track of which session their code went to.

This check makes you sure, every time, where a line of code will run.

## What you will have at the end

- AI features switched off, per the project's house rule
- A Python environment for the certificate that Positron finds on its own
- An R console and a Python console running side by side
- A reliable way to tell which session is active

**Time box:** 40 minutes on top of your lab. The R half is capped at 20.

## How to work this file

- Each task states an outcome. Finding the how is part of the check.
- Where a task asks you to predict, write the prediction before you test it.
- The hint names the Positron docs page to read if you get stuck. Use it only after trying.

Bring that lab's notebook and its data into this repository before you begin. Put them under `coursera/`, in a folder for the course.

## House rule: AI off

AI features are out of scope for this project. Find the settings that switch them off and set them. Positron has a general switch and separate ones for the console, notebooks, and Git commit messages.

*Hint: "Configure AI features". The setting names to look for include `ai.enabled`, `console.assistantActions.enabled`, `notebook.ai.enabled`, and `git.suggestions.enabled`.*

**Which settings did you change, and at user level or folder level?**

## Python half

This repository needs one Python environment that every lab uses. Create it from inside Positron, or confirm the one you already have. Install what your current lab imports.

*Hint: "Discovering Python Installations".*

**Which tool did you choose (uv, venv, or conda), and why?**

Open your lab notebook and confirm it is running on the repository's environment, not on a system Python.

## Checks

- [ ] AI features are off and I know which settings did it
- [ ] The repository has one Python environment and Positron starts it without being told
- [ ] My lab notebook runs on that environment
- [ ] I can run an R console and a Python console together
- [ ] I can say where a line of code will run before I run it
